description: A frog that lives on your Mac desktop and types what you say. On-device dictation, meeting notes, memory, and a voice.

summary.one_liner: Frog is an open-source, on-device Mac desktop pet that dictates what you say into any app, takes meeting notes, and chats back using local models.
summary.what_it_does: Frog runs as a macOS app with a three.js animated frog on the desktop. Holding the fn key records speech and types the transcription at the cursor in whatever app is focused. Starting a meeting session from the frog's menu records both the user and other participants, transcribes them, labels speakers, and writes a summary. Holding right Option opens a voice conversation where the frog answers aloud, stores facts the user tells it, and sets reminders that it speaks when due. A vocabulary feature suggests and learns names and jargon, and correcting a dictation teaches it. Speech recognition, speaker labels, and the language model run locally, with models downloaded on first use. The README says an optional Claude API key can be used for meeting summaries instead of the on-device model; that is the only optional path that sends data off the Mac.
use_cases: dictate prompts to a coding agent
type by voice into any Mac app
keep a local voice assistant with memory
set spoken reminders on a Mac
private alternative to cloud dictation tools
how_to_run: Download Frog.zip from the latest release, unzip, and drag VoicePet.app to Applications
On first launch, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway
Grant Microphone, Speech Recognition, and Accessibility permissions
Set System Settings > Keyboard > 'Press 🌐 key to' to Do Nothing
To build from source: git clone, cd frog, (cd web && npm ci), ./build.sh, then ditto build/VoicePet.app ~/Applications/VoicePet.app and open it
notable: Fully on-device pipeline for speech, speaker labels, and LLM; nothing sent off the Mac unless a Claude API key is added for summaries
Hold fn to dictate into any focused app, aimed at coding agent prompts
Meeting notes capture both sides of a call, label speakers, and write a summary
Memory and spoken reminders, with a Mind tab showing what it knows
Brain model chosen by RAM size, from a 1 GB Qwen option up to a 26B-A4B Gemma model
caveats: Prebuilt release requires macOS 26 on Apple Silicon and is arm64-only
Building from source requires macOS 26, Xcode Command Line Tools, and Node 20.19+ or 22.12+; first build can take several minutes
Intel source builds omit Parakeet transcription and speaker diarization
Speaker diarization is Apple Silicon only
Models download on first use; larger brain models need up to 17 GB
